title: Bringing Enterprise Content into the Pipeline
description: 2026-04-12. I am working on an Alfresco REST connector and its connection to the VALESKA ingestion pipeline.
body:
2026-04-12. I am working on an Alfresco REST connector and its connection to the VALESKA ingestion pipeline.

At this point, the design treats enterprise content as governed source material whose provenance, structure, and permissions matter before extraction begins. The immediate objective is to make the boundary explicit: what enters the system, what is recorded about it, and what remains outside the claim being made.

Why this matters

The implementation is deliberately concrete. the connector is the beginning of an evidence path, not a promise that an external repository can be copied casually or understood without its operating context. This is why the work includes service boundaries, stored records, and repeatable operations rather than a single broad description of “AI memory.” Each layer needs a job that can be inspected.

The implementation does not replace the judgment required to describe a business, a document set, or a working team. It provides a repeatable path for retaining the evidence that judgment uses. A technical decision is useful only when a later reader can see its scope, its constraints, and the result it was intended to support.

What I will test next

The next work will test the boundary in actual practice: whether the records can be retrieved at the right time, whether their provenance remains clear, and whether the system makes a real task easier without overstating what it knows. That distinction will guide the outcome posts that follow.

Historical basis: This entry is dated to the 2026-04-12 repository milestone, commits 91d03c8, 6f1469a. It is based on the contemporaneous implementation records and their documented scope.
